translation:
  text: '“What, then, sir,” I said, “if these people, despite being like this, repent and cast off the
    desires of these women, return to the virgins, and walk in their power and their works? Will they
    not enter God’s house?”[a]


    2. “They will enter,” he said, “if they cast off the works of these women, take up the power of the
    virgins, and walk in their works. That is why construction has been suspended: if these people repent,
    they may go into the building of the tower. But if they do not repent, others will go, and these people
    will be cast out for good.”


    3. For all this I thanked the Lord, because he had compassion on all who call upon his name. He sent
    the messenger of repentance[b] to us who had sinned against him and renewed our spirit. When we were
    already ruined and had no hope of living, he renewed our life.[c]


    4. “Now, sir,” I said, “explain to me why the tower has not been built on the ground, but on the rock
    and the gate.” “You ask because you are foolish and lack understanding,” he said.[d] “Sir,” I said,
    “I have to ask you about everything, because I cannot understand anything at all. Everything is great
    and glorious and difficult for people to understand.”


    5. “Listen,” he said. “The name of the Son of God is great and cannot be contained, and it sustains
    the whole world. So if all creation is sustained through the Son of God, what do you think of those
    called by him, who bear the Son of God’s name and walk in his commandments?[e]”


    6. “Do you see, then, whom he sustains? Those who bear his name with their whole heart. So he became
    their foundation,[f] and he gladly sustains them, because they are not ashamed to bear his name.”'
  philosophy: optimal-equivalence

  - marker: a
    reason: lexical_alternative
    text: The women and virgins are figures in this vision, explained by the names in the next chapter.
      The conditional concerns abandoning one set of desires and works and taking up the other; it is
      not a statement about women as a general class.
  - marker: b
    reason: textual_variant
    text: The singular “messenger” follows the printed working text compared with Latin Vulgata, Palatina
      and Ethiopic; the apparatus reports an irregular plural in Athos. Repentance here includes changed
      conduct and restored hope, not merely a feeling of regret.
  - marker: c

    text: The printed working text reads ἀνενέωσε, “renewed,” with Latin Vulgata and Palatina cited in
      the apparatus. The apparatus reports Athos ἀνένευσε, a form of ἀνανεύω, associated with nodding
      or a gesture of refusal. Its intended sense here is uncertain; the supplied report does not establish

base_translation:
  text: '“What, then, sir,” I said, “if these people, despite being like this, repent and cast off the
    desires of these women, return to the virgins, and walk in their power and their works? Will they
    not enter God’s house?”[a]


    2. “They will enter,” he said, “if they cast off the works of these women, take up the power of the
    virgins, and walk in their works. That is why construction has been suspended: if these people repent,
    they may go into the building of the tower. But if they do not repent, others will go, and these people
    will be cast out for good.”


    3. For all this I thanked the Lord, because he had compassion on all who call upon his name. He sent
    the messenger of repentance[b] to us who had sinned against him and renewed our spirit. When we were
    already ruined and had no hope of living, he renewed our life.[c]


    4. “Now, sir,” I said, “explain to me why the tower has not been built on the ground, but on the rock
    and the gate.” “You ask because you are foolish and lack understanding,” he said.[d] “Sir,” I said,
    “I have to ask you about everything, because I cannot understand anything at all. Everything is great
    and glorious and difficult for people to understand.”


    5. “Listen,” he said. “The name of the Son of God is great and cannot be contained, and it sustains
    the whole world. So if all creation is sustained through the Son of God, what do you think of those
    called by him, who bear the Son of God’s name and walk in his commandments?[e]”


    6. “Do you see, then, whom he sustains? Those who bear his name with their whole heart. So he became
    their foundation,[f] and he gladly sustains them, because they are not ashamed to bear his name.”'
